The Map's Partial Derivatives of the Fifth Order

Source: R/d34e_reparam.R
reparam_map_order5.Rd

Adds to the keyed tables of a reparametrization the partials of the fifth order, each the derivative along its largest coordinate of the partial of the fourth order below it.

Usage

reparam_map_order5(distrib, theta, maps)

Arguments

distrib

A reparametrized family whose reparam_derivs supplies the fourth order.

theta

A named list of the new parameters.

maps

The tables to the fourth order, from reparam_tables().

Value

maps with the partials of the fifth order added under their keys.

Details

The contract of map_derivs stops at the fourth order, and the fourth derivative of the expected information reads the fifth. A partial of the fifth order is the derivative, along one new coordinate \(\phi_c\), of an analytic partial of the fourth order. It is formed by a central difference of the tables at \(\phi_c \pm h\) and at \(\pm h/2\), extrapolated as \((4D(h/2) - D(h))/3\), with \(h\) the relative step \(2\cdot 10^{-4}\) of the coordinate kept inside its bounds by fd_steps(). The tables are closed forms evaluated at four shifted points per coordinate, with no evaluation of the parent, and the difference is taken once on an analytic quantity.
